The Court made the following:
ORDER:

The present Writ Petition is filed by the petitioners seeking to declare the Arbitration Award Nos.30 and 31 of 2014, dated 19.12.2014 passed by the 2nd respondent and the Award No.78/2012-13,
dated 01.09.2012, passed by the 3rd respondent, as illegal, arbitrary, violative of provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956 and for consequential directions.

2) Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners.
Also heard the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition and the learned Standing Counsel for the National Highways Authority of India.
3) Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners owned an extent of Ac.0-33  cents each in Sy.No.32 of Idamadaka Revenue Village, Duvvuru Mandal of Kadapa District.

Pursuant to the proposal for widening of NH-18 Road from Km.167.750 to 224.360 (Kadapa to Kurnool) in Idamadaka Village, learned counsel submits that the petitioners' lands were acquired as per the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956 (for short "the NH Act") and the 3rd respondent fixed the value of the land at the rate of Rs.5,00,000/- per acre and accordingly the petitioners' land was valued at the rate of Rs.1,67,500/- each.

He submits that the petitioners received the compensation amount under protest and initiated Arbitration proceedings before the 2nd respondent- District Collector for enhancement of compensation as determined by the 3rd respondent-Joint Collector.

He submits that before the 2nd respondent it was inter alia, contended that the value of the land is Rs.40,00,000/- per acre by producing relevant material, but the 2nd respondent without proper appreciation of the petitioners' contentions enhanced the compensation from Rs.5,00,000/- to Rs.7,00,000/- only per acre vide Arbitration Award Nos.30 and 31 of 2014,
dated 19.12.2014.

Learned counsel submits that the value of the lands acquired for the purpose of laying roads is more than Rs.40,00,000/- per acre and that the petitioners' lands are abutting NJS,J WP_21535_2015 the Highway and near to the town, but the 2nd respondent had failed to consider the matter in a proper perspective.

He submits that the 3rd respondent as well as the 2nd respondent has committed material irregularity in fixing the lower value in respect of the lands in question and the Awards are illegal, in as much as the value of the land situated in the vicinity of the petitioners' lands has not been taken into account.
He submits that by virtue of the impugned Awards in fixing the lower market value, the petitioners suffer serious prejudice and irreparable loss.

4) On the other hand, the learned counsel for the 4th respondent while justifying the fixation of the value of the land by the 2 nd respondent contends that the Writ Petition is not maintainable in the light of the specific provisions of the NH Act.
He submits that against the Award passed by the Arbitrator-2nd respondent, the petitioners have to approach the competent jurisdictional Civil Court.
In elaboration, he submits that in terms of Section 3G(6) of the NH Act, the provisions of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 are applicable to every arbitration under the NH Act.

He submits that if the petitioners have any grievance in respect of the Awards passed by the 2nd respondent, the only remedy is to invoke the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and challenge the Awards under Section 34 of the said Act.
He submits that in view of the availability of the efficacious alternative remedy, the Writ Petition is liable to be dismissed.
On appreciation of the rival contentions, this Court finds merits in the submissions made by the learned counsel for the 4th respondent.

Section 3G of the NH Act contemplates determination of the amount payable as compensation and provides that where any land is acquired under the NH Act,
the amount as determined by an order of the competent authority shall be paid.

2 NH Act contemplates that if the amount determined by the competent authority under Sub-Section (1) or Sub-Section (2) is not acceptable to either of the parties, the amount shall, on an application by either of the parties, be determined by the arbitrator to be appointed by the Central Government.
It is not in dispute that the concerned District Collectors are the arbitrators appointed in terms of the provisions of NH Act.
As per Section 3G(6) of the NH Act, the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act shall apply to every arbitration under the provisions of the NH Act.

As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the 4th respondent, in view of the applicability of the provisions of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the challenge to the Awards passed under the provisions of the NH Act has to be laid before a competent jurisdictional Civil Court.

However,
in the present case, the petitioners straight away filed the present Writ Petition challenging the Awards passed by the 2nd respondent.
When the specific remedies are available as per the statute invocation of the jurisdiction of this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India is not tenable.
Learned counsel for the petitioners has not raised any other NJS,J WP_21535_2015 contention justifying the invocation of the extraordinary jurisdiction of this Court.

6) Considering the matter in its entirety and in the light of the statutory provisions referred to supra,
this Court has no hesitation to hold that the Writ Petition against the impugned Awards is not maintainable and is inclined to dispose of the Writ Petition leaving it open to the petitioners to work out their remedies against the Awards in question, in accordance with law.
7) Accordingly, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
No order as to costs.
8) Consequently, the Miscellaneous Applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.

NINALA JAYASURYA, J Date: 10.07.2024 SSV NJS,J WP_21535_2015 THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE NINALA JAYASURYA Date: 10.07.2024 SSV B.Narasimha Rao, S/O Venkataramanaiah ... vs State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151257031/
